{{Current events|year=2019|month=03|day=1|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Business and economy
*[[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] announces plans to open dozens of proprietary grocery stores in several major U.S. cities. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/amazon-to-launch-new-grocery-store-business-sources-say-11551461887 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]  [http://fortune.com/2019/03/01/amazon-may-launch-a-new-chain-of-grocery-stores/ (''Fortune'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*A bus overturns on the [[Qom]]–[[Tehran]] Highway in [[Iran]], killing eight people (including the driver) and injuring more than thirty others. Officials claim the driver fell asleep. [https://www.france24.com/en/20190301-8-dead-iran-bus-accident (France 24)]
*A [[Russia]]n cargo ship collides with a motorway bridge in the city of [[Busan]], [[South Korea]]. The captain is reported to be drunk. [https://www.theguardian.com/global/video/2019/mar/01/russian-cargo-ship-crashes-into-bridge-in-south-korea-video (The Guardian)]
;International relations
*[[Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh]]
**[[Bangladesh]]'s Foreign Secretary Shahidul Haque tells the [[United Nations Security Council]] that his country will no longer accept [[Rohingya people|Rohingya]] refugees fleeing violence across the border in [[Rakhine State]], and accuses [[Myanmar]] of "hollow promises" regarding [[repatriation]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-47412704 (BBC)]
*[[South Korea–United States relations]]
**The [[United States Armed Forces]] is preparing to announce that annual large-scale joint exercises conducted with [[South Korea]] every spring will no longer be held. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/military/u-s-end-large-scale-military-drills-south-korea-n978111 (NBC News)]
*[[North Korea–Vietnam relations]]
**North Korean [[Supreme Leader of North Korea|leader]] [[Kim Jong-un]] kicks off an official visit to [[Vietnam]], three days after arriving in the country for a nuclear summit with [[United States|U.S.]] [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] that ended in deadlock. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/north-korean-leader-kim-jong-un-kicks-off-official-vietnam-visit (''The Straits Times'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 United States presidential election]], [[2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries]]
**[[Government of the State of Washington|Washington Governor]] [[Jay Inslee]] announces he will join the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] primaries in 2020 and cites [[Climate change mitigation|fighting climate change]] as a reason. [http://time.com/5539302/jay-inslee-climate-change/ (''Time'')] [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/03/01/us/jay-inslee-2020.html (''The New York Times'')]
